programs.title: Governing the Algorithmic Workplace: DAO Skills for Worker Leaders
outcomes: Explain how agent-managed, human-governed DAOs separate agent operations from human-reserved decisions
Draft a workplace governance charter that keeps hiring, pay and discipline votes in human hands
Evaluate AI monitoring and task-routing systems using evidence summaries
Practice collective decision-making in a proposal forum format

sessions.activity: Study the DAO charter model: mission, contribution model, measurable outcomes; map which workplace decisions must remain human-reserved.
Review sample evidence summaries on AI in the workplace; practice spotting unsupported claims and asking critical questions of agent outputs.
Role-play a decision cycle: agents draft proposals, members debate and vote; compare outcomes to traditional collective bargaining processes.
Working-group exercise: design task-routing rules so AI coordinates work but never overrides worker protections.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized proposals and vote patterns (no names, no employer identifiers) contributed to a shared model of democratic decision practices.
programs.consent: Voluntary opt-in at enrollment with written plain-language notice; learners may participate fully without contributing data and may withdraw shared data at any time.

programs.title: Virtual Worlds on Real Wetlands: Civics and Ecology of the Metaverse
outcomes: Locate Meta HQ at 1 Hacker Way, Menlo Park on a map and describe its bayfront wetland setting
Explain what a DAO is and why humans keep the most important votes
Compare virtual worlds with the real ecosystems they are built upon
Draft a simple class charter with measurable outcomes

sessions.activity: Read the DAO's charter and mission; students draft a classroom charter listing decisions only humans in the class may vote on.
Using maps of San Francisco Bay, students investigate how the Menlo Park bayfront wetland was restored and why it matters.
Students propose a class project to help a local wetland or digital-civics goal; peers debate, then the class holds a final human vote.
Students set measurable outcomes for their project and build a simple chart tracking progress over the term.

programs.data_shared: Anonymous class-level project outcomes and progress charts (no student names or identifying details) added to a shared civics-education examples library.
programs.consent: Guardian/parent signed consent plus student assent required before any data contribution; all data is class-level and anonymous, and families may opt out without affecting participation.

programs.title: Agent-Assisted, Human-Governed: DAO Models for Civil Society
programs.grade_or_level: Professional / NGO staff and program managers
outcomes: Assess whether an agent-managed DAO structure fits their organization's mission
Design evidence-monitoring and synthesis workflows using AI agents
Build a proposal pipeline where agents draft and humans decide
Define measurable outcomes aligned with a public-good mission

sessions.activity: Analyze the charter structure: mission, contribution model, measurable outcomes; workshop a mission-aligned charter for participants' own NGOs.
Hands-on with evidence monitoring: participants structure a research question and outline how agents would summarize evidence for stewards.
Proposal clinic: participants draft proposals in the agent role, then switch to the human role to debate, amend and decide.
Design task-routing and working-group structures for cross-team coordination between decision cycles.
Build a progress-tracking dashboard template tied to the charter's measurable outcomes.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized charter drafts and outcome frameworks (organization names removed) shared as open templates in a civil-society governance library.
programs.consent: Organizational consent via signed data-sharing agreement; individual participants opt in separately; identifying details stripped before sharing.

programs.title: From Mission to Measurable Outcomes: Nonprofit Governance in an Agent-Managed DAO
outcomes: Translate a nonprofit mission into measurable, trackable outcomes
Clarify which governance actions stay with the human board (votes, amendments, treasury, appointments)
Use agent-drafted proposals to speed board decision cycles without ceding authority
Track and report progress transparently to funders and members

sessions.activity: Map the nonprofit's mission onto a charter with explicit human-reserved actions: final votes, amendments, treasury transfers, appointments.
Simulation: agents present drafted grant proposals; the board debates and holds the final human vote on enactment.
Design working groups and task routing for staff and volunteers between board meetings.
Create a progress report against the charter's outcomes, suitable for funders, using tracking examples from the DAO model.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized outcome metrics and progress-report templates (no beneficiary or donor data) contributed to a shared nonprofit governance benchmark set.
programs.consent: Board-approved participation policy; no personal or beneficiary data collected; all shared metrics are aggregated and de-identified, with withdrawal available on request.
